p: Thickened with pig-iron rivets and provincial stubbornness.
Heavy enough to leave ruts in the frontier mud.
Forged by men who died of stone-lung before thirty.
It does not fit a human shoulder; the shoulder must adapt.
Keeps the marsh-fever fog at bay for another hour.
Notched with tiny, obsessive tally marks in the margin.
Smells faintly of snuffed church tallow and cold stone.
Hums with a geometry that makes the teeth ache.
Lightened by paring away every ounce of ornament.
Made for couriers who are paid only if they survive.
The leather whistles sharply when swung against the wind.
Smells of boiled leather and willow-bark poultice.
Retains the heat of its previous owner's final fever.
Stitched with cured salt-marsh tendon that refuses to part.
The heart keeps beating long after the mind begs it to stop.
Condensation gathers on the rim even in the dry wastes.
Hollowed out to hold more aether than is strictly safe.
Buried for seven winters beneath a cracked border cairn.
Staring into the polish reveals stars that died centuries ago.
Patched with boilerplate from a dismantled river barge.
Stamped with the quartermaster's seal of Oakhaven.
Turns aside crossbow quarrels with a dull, indifferent thud.
Balanced to compensate for a trembling, gin-soaked hand.
Finds the gap between gorget and collarbone without being asked.
Greased with mutton tallow against the icy river shallows.
Worn by sentries who chipped frost from their eyelids at dawn.
Cold no longer bites the flesh; it merely recognizes kin.
Blackened in the coal pits outside Thornwick.
Baked until the metal forgot how to melt.
Quenched in the ash-choked vents beneath Ironcamp.
Stained yellow by decades of wading through stagnant peat.
Crusted with bitter desert alkali that neutralizes venom.
Steeped in mithridate until the wearer's spit turns bitter.
Threaded with cheap copper wire that trails into the dirt.
Set with hollow glass tubes fused where lightning struck the dunes.
Drinks the tempest and leaves only the smell of ozone.
Nicknamed by a cutthroat who never fought fair in his life.
Designed for dismemberment rather than honorable dueling.
Every edge is honed to seek the softest part of a man.
Requires only one clean stroke to settle an argument.
Drinks modestly from the cut, leaving the wound oddly pale.
The hilt grows warm and slick the longer the melee drags on.
Collects what is owed in crimson coin.
It does not merely drink; it demands a second course.
Steadies the breathing when the shields begin to splinter.
Slowly refills itself from the damp air of the world.
Ticks with a rhythmic, unseen momentum.
What is spent in fire returns in smoke.
